title: How much bigger does it get?

text.guided:
A matrix moves the whole plane, so it also changes **areas**. Every area in the plane is multiplied by the same number: the **determinant**.

If î is stretched to (2, 0) and ĵ to (0, 3), the unit square becomes a 2 by 3 rectangle: its area is 6, so the determinant is 6.
text.fast: $\det M$ is the factor by which $M$ scales areas. For a diagonal matrix it is the product of the stretches.

examples.games: Zoom a map 2× wider and 3× taller: every region takes 6 times more screen.
examples.physics: Stretch a rubber sheet by 2 in one direction and 1.5 in the other: every patch grows by 3 times.
examples.sport: Widen the pitch 2× and lengthen it 3×: every zone of the pitch covers 6 times more grass.

robot: The press changes every area by the same factor. That factor is the determinant.

mission.games: The power-up makes sprites 2× wider and 1.5× taller. Bet on the new area.
mission.physics: The fluid is stretched 2× and 1.5×. How much more space does it fill?
mission.sport: The pitch gets 2× longer and 1.5× wider. How many times more grass?

title: Negative means flipped

text.guided:
Sometimes the plane is turned over like a page: î and ĵ swap sides. The area is the same size, but the shape is a mirror image. We record that with a **negative** determinant.

So |det| is the size of the area factor, and the sign says whether the plane was flipped.
text.fast: $\det M < 0$ means $M$ reverses orientation. $|\det M|$ is the area factor.

examples.games: Mirror your level horizontally: same size, but left and right are swapped.
examples.physics: A reflection in a mirror keeps lengths and areas but reverses handedness.
examples.sport: Play the second half on the other side: same pitch size, but left and right wings are swapped.

robot: A negative determinant means the press flipped the shape over. Same size, mirror image.

mission.games: This press mirrors the level. Bet on the area, sign included.
mission.physics: Swap the two axes: same area, but which sign?
mission.sport: Switch wings at half-time. Same pitch size, but what sign?

title: Zero: crushed flat

text.guided:
If both arrows end up on the same line, the plane is **crushed flat**: every shape becomes a line segment, with area 0. The determinant is 0.

That is also why a determinant of 0 is bad news: once the plane is flattened, you cannot tell where each point came from.
text.fast: $\det M = 0$ iff the columns are linearly dependent: the image is a line (or a point) and $M$ is not invertible.

examples.games: Squash a character against the wall until it is a line: you can no longer tell its height.
examples.physics: Projecting a 3D object onto a flat screen loses depth: the lost dimension cannot be recovered.
examples.sport: Squash the whole pitch onto the halfway line: you can no longer tell how far up the field a player was.

robot: Determinant zero: the press flattens everything onto a line. Nothing has area any more.

check.prompt: The matrix [[1, 2], [2, 4]] sends î to (1, 2) and ĵ to (2, 4). What happens to the plane?
options: It is crushed onto a line
